page: Microsoft Azure E8as_v4 is an EASv4-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU runs at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 131 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the top 25% at 2706.79. Memory performance is also a highlight, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top 25%. Most other metrics, including Geekbench multi-core (6347.0), Passmark CPU (12006.7), and Redis SET operations (8.2 million ops/sec), fall within the average tier. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and prompt processing for medium (7B) LLM models show weaker relative performance, placing in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density of 8 GB per vCPU, the E8as_v4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. The balance of a strong single-core CPU and high memory capacity makes it well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise applications, and moderate data processing tasks. It is less optimal for highly parallelized, compute-intensive tasks or large-scale LLM inference due to its average multi-core and weak multi-threaded decompression benchmarks.
